subject: community-medicine
title: Hypertension: Rule of Halves, Classification and Population Control

steps.title: Rule of halves: the iceberg in numbers
steps.tx: The **rule of halves** states that in a typical community only about half of hypertensives are detected, half of those detected are treated, and half of those treated are controlled, leaving roughly one in eight adequately managed. Modern surveys improve the fractions unevenly, but the cascade shape remains the fastest community diagnosis in NCD teaching.
steps.say: Half, half, half. Half detected, half of those treated, half of those controlled: one in eight managed. Fractions improve unevenly across surveys, but the cascade still diagnoses a community fastest.

nodes.label: Half of those controlled: one eighth

steps.title: Classification by office readings
steps.tx: **Hypertension classification** in common Indian teaching (JNC lineage) reads normal under 120/80, prehypertension or elevated bands above it, stage 1 at 140 to 159/90 to 99, stage 2 at 160/100 and beyond, with 140/90 the diagnostic threshold on repeated measurement. Newer American thresholds at 130/80 create stem ambiguity, so answers should name the classification system used.
steps.say: Thresholds need naming. One forty over ninety diagnoses in classic teaching on repeated readings; stage two begins at one sixty over one hundred. Newer American cut-offs differ, so state your system in answers.

steps.title: Measurement technique decides truth
steps.tx: **Measurement error** manufactures hypertension and misses it: 5 minutes rest seated, back supported, feet flat, arm at heart level, correct cuff size (bladder encircling most of the arm), no talking, no recent caffeine or smoking, and two readings averaged, repeated on another day before labelling. White-coat and masked hypertension explain discordance with home and ambulatory monitoring.
steps.say: Technique decides truth. Seated rest, supported arm at heart level, right cuff, silence, two readings averaged, another day before labelling. White-coat and masked patterns explain office-home discordance examiners love.

steps.title: Population strategy: shift the whole curve
steps.tx: **Salt reduction** is the population flagship: cutting average intake toward 5 grams daily shifts the entire blood pressure distribution left, preventing more events than treating severe cases alone, Geoffrey Rose's prevention paradox applied. Potassium-rich diets, weight control, alcohol moderation and activity complete the primordial layer the NPCDCS health promotion arm preaches.
steps.say: Shift the whole curve. Salt toward five grams daily moves average pressure left and prevents more events than rescuing severe cases. Rose's paradox in action: many at small risk outnumber few at high risk.

left.title: Population approach
points: Small average fall, huge event saving

steps.title: Opportunistic screening at 30 years
steps.tx: **NPCDCS screening** offers blood pressure (with glucose) measurement to all adults 30 years and above at health facilities and community screening camps, because yield justifies the age floor and younger hypertension is rarer. Detected cases enter NCD clinics at PHC and CHC levels with drug supply and follow-up registers, converting camps into chronic care rather than case counts.
steps.say: Thirty is the screening floor. Pressure and glucose for every adult above it, at facilities and camps, feeding NCD clinics with registers and drug supply. Camps must convert into chronic care, not case counts.

steps.title: Tracking, target organ damage, referral
steps.tx: **Tracking phenomenon** means children in high blood pressure percentiles tend to stay high as adults, justifying school and adolescent measurement in high-risk families. Established hypertension is staged by target organ damage (heart, kidney, retina, brain) deciding referral urgency. Resistant hypertension on three drugs including a diuretic triggers secondary-cause evaluation.
steps.say: Pressure tracks from childhood percentiles into adult ranks. Target organ damage stages urgency in the established case. Resistance on three drugs including a diuretic demands secondary cause hunting.

steps.title: Lifestyle prescription with numbers
steps.tx: **Non-drug therapy** quantifies: weight loss lowers systolic roughly 1 mmHg per kilogram in teaching estimates, DASH-style diet rich in fruit, vegetables and low-fat dairy, sodium restriction, 30 minutes activity most days, alcohol limits, tobacco cessation absolutely. Every drug prescription without this prescription wastes half the consultation, examiners note, because effects add to pharmacotherapy.
steps.say: Prescribe lifestyle in numbers. Kilogram for millimetre in teaching estimates, DASH plates, thirty active minutes most days, alcohol capped, tobacco zero. Drug scripts without lifestyle scripts waste half the consultation.

steps.title: Drug therapy principles in programme care
steps.tx: **First-line classes** (thiazide-type diuretics, calcium channel blockers, ACE inhibitors or ARBs, with beta blockers for compelling indications) start singly or in combination by level and comorbidity: ACE or ARB compulsory flavour in diabetes with albuminuria, avoided in pregnancy where ACE and ARB are teratogenic. Free drug supply through public facilities decides adherence more than molecule choice at population scale.
steps.say: Classes first, brands last. Thiazides, calcium blockers, ACE or ARB families start therapy; pregnancy forbids the last two. At population scale free supply decides adherence more than molecule elegance.

left.title: Compelling preferences
points: Diabetes with albuminuria: ACE or ARB
Older isolated systolic: CCB or thiazide

steps.title: Hypertensive emergencies versus urgencies
steps.tx: **Hypertensive emergency** couples severe elevation with acute target organ damage (encephalopathy, pulmonary oedema, dissection, eclampsia) needing controlled intravenous reduction in monitored units, while urgency without damage takes oral therapy and hours-to-days reduction. Dropping pressure precipitously in chronic hypertension strokes watershed territories, the balancing error stems test at the bedside.
steps.say: Damage, not numbers, defines emergency. Acute organ injury takes monitored intravenous control; no damage takes oral therapy over hours to days. Precipitous drops stroke watershed brain in chronic hypertensives.
